name: AI Overview Part 2

chatHistory.content: Part 1: Raw Description (Shot-by-Shot) Phase 1: Compare the Three Engines (0:00:00:00 – 0:00:17:08 · Frames 0–433) Beats covered: 1–4 Visual concept: Three large engine panels appear side by side horizontally, each showing the same query but with different AI-generated answers and different citation sources. This is the core "compare" moment — the viewer sees at a glance that the same question yields different citations depending on the engine. Layout: Three cards of equal width (~950px each) sit horizontally centered in the safe zone with 40px gaps. Each card has: A header bar with the engine name (Google AI Mode / Perplexity / ChatGPT) in blue, uppercase, weight 800, 32px, with a subtle bottom border A mock AI answer area: 3 skeleton lines (90%, 75%, 82% width) at 13px height inside a subtle blue-tinted container (rgba(0,170,255,0.05)) A "Citations" label below (22px, muted, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.1em) 3 citation pill rows beneath, each pill is a domain name Citation pills color logic: Domains that appear in ALL three engines (e.g. "techcrunch.com", "wired.com"): green-tinted pill (rgba(74,222,128,0.1) fill, rgba(74,222,128,0.3) border, green text), with a small "ALL ✓" badge at the right edge Domains unique to ONE engine (e.g. "blog.example.com"): amber-tinted pill "yourbrand.io" appears ONLY in the first panel (Google AI Mode): red-tinted pill (rgba(239,68,68,0.08) fill, rgba(239,68,68,0.2) border, red text) Engine citation assignments: Google AI Mode: techcrunch.com (green), wired.com (green), yourbrand.io (red — your brand, only here) Perplexity: techcrunch.com (green), wired.com (green), blog.example.com (amber) ChatGPT: techcrunch.com (green), blog.example.com (amber), wired.com (green) Animation sequence: Frame 0: Scene begins. Background visible. Frames 5–25 (beat 1 starts): Panel 1 (Google AI Mode) fades in + translateY from 50px below. Spring delay 10 relative to phase start. Frames 17–37: Panel 2 (Perplexity) fades in, stagger 12 frames after panel 1. Frames 29–49: Panel 3 (ChatGPT) fades in, stagger 12 frames after panel 2. Frames 70–120 (beat 2 region): Citation pills inside each panel fade in with stagger — the green "ALL ✓" pills animate first (spring delay ~70), then amber pills (~85), then the red "yourbrand.io" pill (~100). Each pill fades in + translateX from 30px. Frames 200–250 (beat 3 finishes): All pills are now visible. A connector/highlight effect draws the viewer's attention to the differences — a subtle pulse glow on the red pill in panel 1, and a "⚠ YOUR BRAND NOT CITED" warning badge fades in below panels 2 and 3 (or just panel 2, centered). The warning is red-tinted, pulsing at a sine wave (0.4 amplitude + 0.6 base), 22px font, bold, letter-spacing 0.05em. Frames 337–433 (beat 4): A color-coded legend fades in at the bottom of the scene: three dots (green = "Cited in all engines", amber = "Cited in one engine", red = "Your brand — missing"), each with a 20px colored circle and 26px muted label. This appears via spring delay ~340, translateY from 20px. Takeaway for viewer: The same query produces different citations in each engine. Your brand might be cited in one but completely absent from another. Phase 2: Look at the Sources (0:00:18:00 – 0:00:36:13 · Frames 450–913) Beats covered: 5–10 Visual concept: This phase shifts focus to analyzing which domains are authoritative. We show a single large card that acts as an "authority analysis" panel. On the left, a ranked list of domains sorted by how many engines cited them. On the right, a breakdown of what makes those top sources different (structure, depth, citations, format) shown as labeled attribute bars. Layout: One wide card spanning the full safe zone width, vertically centered Card: standard card style (rgba(255,255,255,0.05), 2px border, radius 32px, padding 56px 72px) Left half (~55% width): "Top Cited Domains" section Header: "Authoritative Sources" in 28px, muted, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.15em Below: a vertical list of 5 domain rows: techcrunch.com — 3/3 engines (green bar fills 100%) wired.com — 3/3 engines (green bar fills 100%) blog.example.com — 2/3 engines (amber bar fills 66%) yourbrand.io — 1/3 engines (red bar fills 33%) random.org — 0/3 (empty bar, muted text) Each row: domain name (26px, white or muted), a horizontal bar (48px tall, rounded, fills to percentage), a fraction label "3/3" or "2/3" etc. in the bar's accent color Right half (~45% width): "What They Do Differently" section Header: "Content Attributes" in 28px, muted, uppercase Four horizontal attribute bars: "Structure" — 88% fill, blue "Depth" — 76% fill, blue "Citations" — 64% fill, green "Format" — 72% fill, amber Each bar: label on left (200px, 26px, white), horizontal bar (48px height, rounded), percentage on right (26px, accent color) Animation sequence: Phase starts at global frame ~450 (local frame 0 within this phase). Frames 0–20: The card container fades in + translateY from 40px, scale from 0.92. Frames 20–40 (beat 5: "look at the sources"): "Authoritative Sources" header fades in. Frames 40–120 (beats 6-7): Domain rows animate in one by one, staggered by 15 frames. Each row: fade in + translateX from -40px. The bar fills animate with a slight delay after the row appears (bar width interpolates from 0% to target over ~30 frames). Frames 130–180: The green "3/3" rows get a subtle glow pulse to emphasize they're the authority winners. Frames 200–280 (beat 8: "If you're not among them, analyze why"): The "yourbrand.io" row gets highlighted — a red pulsing border appears around it, and a small "⚠" icon fades in next to it. Simultaneously, the right-side "Content Attributes" header fades in. Frames 280–430 (beats 9-10): The four attribute bars on the right animate in, staggered by 18 frames. Each bar label appears first, then the bar fills to its percentage over ~35 frames. On the final beat ("depth, citations, or format, and adapt"), each attribute label briefly brightens (opacity pulses from 0.7 to 1.0) as if being "called out." Takeaway for viewer: Certain domains dominate AI citations across all engines. If you're not among them, you need to analyze what those pages do better in structure, depth, and format. Phase 3: Track Changes Over Time (0:00:36:20 – 0:00:52:00 · Frames 920–1300) Beats covered: 11–15 Visual concept: A line chart showing citation frequency over 12 weeks, with a dramatic "volatility" visualization. Two lines — one for "Competitor A" (blue, solid) that fluctuates significantly, and one for "You" (muted, dashed) that stays flat and low. A large "40–60%" stat animates in to emphasize citation churn. Then a "snapshot vs. scheduled" comparison appears. Layout: Full-width card, vertically centered, same card style as previous phases Inside the card: Header: "AI Citation Frequency — Last 12 Weeks" in 32px, muted, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.08em Chart area: SVG, full width of card (~3000px), 560px tall 5 horizontal grid lines at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% (rgba(255,255,255,0.05), strokeWidth 2) Blue solid line (Competitor A): starts high (~75%), drops steadily to ~6% — dramatic decline showing volatility. StrokeWidth 8, blue, round caps. Muted dashed line (You): hovers flat around 82-84% the whole time — consistent but low citation count. StrokeWidth 6, muted, dash pattern 24 12. NOTE: The Y axis is inverted in the SVG (0 at top), so "high citation" = low Y value X-axis labels: "Wk 1", "Wk 3", "Wk 5", "Wk 7", "Wk 9", "Wk 12" in 28px muted Below the chart: two annotation badges side by side "Competitor A: cited 12×" — blue-tinted badge (rgba(0,170,255,0.1) bg, blue border, 30px, bold), with a 40px solid blue line swatch "You: cited 2×" — muted badge, with a 40px dashed muted line swatch Stat callout: Between the header and the chart (or overlaid on the right side of the chart), a large animated stat: "40–60%" in 96px, weight 900, white with blue glow, with subtitle "of citations change month to month" in 32px muted below it. Animation sequence: Frames 0–20 (beat 11: "track changes over time"): Card container fades in + translateY from 50px. Frames 20–25: Chart header fades in. Frames 25–120 (beat 12-13): Both lines draw progressively from left to right. Use interpolate on frame to control draw progress from 0 to 1. The lines draw simultaneously. As the blue line drops dramatically, it visually tells the volatility story. Frames 80–110: The "40–60%" stat fades in with a scale-up from 0.7, positioned in the upper-right area of the chart or above it. Subtitle fades in 15 frames after. Frames 120–160 (beat 13 ending): Lines fully drawn. Grid lines visible. Frames 160–220 (beat 14: "only checking once, only seeing a snapshot"): A vertical dashed line appears at one point on the chart (e.g., Wk 5) with a label "Snapshot" and a red X or warning indicator — showing that a single check gives incomplete data. Frames 230–300 (beat 15: "scheduled runs give you the full picture"): The "Snapshot" indicator fades out and is replaced by a green highlight bar that spans the entire X-axis width, labeled "Scheduled monitoring" with a green checkmark. The annotation badges below the chart fade in — "Competitor A: cited 12×" (spring delay ~250) and "You: cited 2×" (spring delay ~265). Takeaway for viewer: AI citations are volatile — 40–60% change monthly. A single check is just a snapshot. Scheduled monitoring reveals the real picture. Phase 4: Regional Data (0:00:52:00 – 0:01:07:17 · Frames 1300–1692) Beats covered: 16–20 Visual concept: A world map with three glowing pins — United States, Germany, Japan — each with a card showing the different AI answer citations for that region. This directly illustrates that the same query returns different results in different markets. Layout: World map SVG loaded from assets/other/world.svg, scaled to fill most of the safe zone Map styling: inverted + hue-rotated for dark theme (filter: invert(1) sepia(1) saturate(2) hue-rotate(180deg)), opacity 0.4 Radial gradient overlay: rgba(0,170,255,0.06) at center, transparent at 70% Three map pins at approximate positions: United States: x=22%, y=40% Germany: x=51%, y=30% Japan: x=80%, y=38% Each pin: 48px blue circle with 5px rgba(0,170,255,0.4) border, glow shadow (0 0 36px rgba(0,170,255,0.7)), plus a 4px-wide 32px-tall stem below Each pin has a card floating above it: Card: navy fill (#16213E), 2.5px blue border (rgba(0,170,255,0.45)), radius 24px, padding 32px 44px, min-width 480px Country name: 30px, blue, weight 800, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.08em 2 skeleton lines below (mock AI answer) 2 citation pills: green-tinted, showing region-specific domains US: "techcrunch.com", "wired.com" Germany: "spiegel.de", "heise.de" Japan: "nikkei.com", "asahi.com" Footer callout: Below the map, a wide banner: "Same query · Different AI citations · Every market" in 44px, blue, weight 700, inside a blue-tinted card (rgba(0,170,255,0.08), 2px blue border, radius 20px, padding 32px 96px). Animation sequence: Frames 0–20 (beat 16: "use the regional data"): Map fades in + scale from 0.9. Radial gradient overlay appears. Frames 40–60 (beat 17 start): US pin drops in — scale from 0 + translateY from -30px, spring delay 40. Frames 65–85: Germany pin drops in — spring delay 65. Frames 90–110 (beat 18: "US versus Germany versus Japan"): Japan pin drops in — spring delay 90. Frames 75–150: Region cards fade in above their respective pins, staggered ~35 frames after each pin appears. Each card: scale from 0.7 + translateY from 30px. Citation pills inside each card fade in as the card settles. Frames 200–300 (beats 19-20: "international campaigns... localization issues"): The footer banner fades in + translateY from 30px. Spring delay ~250 relative to phase start. Takeaway for viewer: AI citations vary by region. International campaigns need per-market monitoring to catch localization gaps. Phase 5: Closing Statement (0:01:08:05 – 0:01:14:19 · Frames 1705–1869) Beats covered: 21–22 Visual concept: A powerful, minimal closing screen. Two lines of text, centered, with the second line emphasizing the key message. No cards, no charts — just typography against the background. Layout: Centered vertically and horizontally in the safe zone Line 1: "SEO is no longer just about ranking on page one." in 52px, weight 600, muted color, with a slight opacity (0.7). This line sets up the contrast. Line 2: "It's about being the source LLMs trust enough to cite." in 64px, weight 800, white with a subtle blue gradient (white to #00AAFF at 135deg), applied as background-clip text. This is the punchline. A thin horizontal gradient line (blue, transparent at edges) separates the two lines, ~600px wide, 3px tall. Animation sequence: Frames 0–15 (beat 21 start): Line 1 fades in + translateY from 30px below. Frames 15–30: Horizontal divider line draws from 0 to 600px width. Frames 30–50 (beat 22 starts): Line 2 fades in + translateY from 30px, scale from 0.92 to 1. Slightly slower spring for gravitas. Frames 50–164: Hold. Both lines visible. Subtle pulse glow on line 2 (sine wave on text-shadow or opacity, very gentle). Closing Black (Frames ~1890–1910) ~20 frames of solid black (#000000), fading in from the last phase via the standard fade transition. Part 2: Remotion Code-Gen Prompt Create a single continuous Remotion composition (3840×2160, 25fps, total duration approximately 1910 frames) for an Apify YouTube video b-roll animation. Design system: Background: background_blue.png via staticFile("assets/backgrounds/background_blue.png"), rendered as a full-canvas with objectFit: "cover" behind all content in every phase. Safe zone: position absolute, left 250px, top 250px, width 3340px, height 1660px, overflow hidden. All animated content lives inside this wrapper. Color palette (use exact values): bg: #1A1A2E (fallback only) navy: #16213E (card backgrounds, secondary panels) blue: #00AAFF (primary accent, Apify brand) green: #4ADE80 (positive, "cited in all", checkmarks) amber: #FBBF24 (warnings, single-engine citations) red: #EF4444 (negative, "not cited", expensive) muted: #9CA3AF (secondary text, labels) white: #FFFFFF (primary text) card: rgba(255,255,255,0.05) (card fill) cardBorder: rgba(255,255,255,0.08) (card stroke) Font: Inter. Hierarchy: display 280-320px/900, subtitles 48-64px/500-700, card headers 28-32px/700-800 uppercase blue with letter-spacing 0.06-0.15em, body 22-30px/600-700 muted, smallest text 36px minimum for 4K readability. Motion: spring({ damping: 200 }) for all entrances. Stagger sequential elements by 12-18 frames. Transitions between phases: fade() with linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 17 }). Use useCurrentFrame() and interpolate() for progressive draws and timing. Use spring() for element entrances. No floating section headings. The voiceover provides context. Center content in safe zone unless layout dictates otherwise. Panel 2 fades in: spring delay 22, translateY from 50px. Panel 3 fades in: spring delay 34, translateY from 50px. Citation pills inside all panels fade in with spring delay starting at 70, staggered by 12 frames per pill, translateX from 30px, scale from 0.7. Red-tinted card (rgba(239,68,68,0.12), 1.5px border rgba(239,68,68,0.4), radius 14px, padding 14px 20px, 22px red text, weight 700, centered, letter-spacing 0.05em). PHASE 2 — Look at the Sources (Sequence duration: 480 + 17 = 497 frames) One full-width card centered in the safe zone. Card style: card fill/border, radius 32px, padding 56px 72px. Inside, a two-column layout using flex row. Left column (~55% width): "Authoritative Sources" Header: "Authoritative Sources" in 28px, muted, uppercase, weight 700, letter-spacing 0.15em, marginBottom 36px. 5 domain rows stacked vertically with 20px gap. Each row is a flex row: Domain name: 26px, weight 700, white (or muted for low-ranked), minWidth 340px, text-align right. Horizontal bar: 48px height, rgba(255,255,255,0.05) background, radius 24px, flex 1, overflow hidden. Inside, a colored fill div with width as percentage, same height, matching accent color, radius 24px, opacity 0.8. Fraction label: 26px, weight 800, accent color, minWidth 80px. Data: techcrunch.com — 100% — "3/3" — green wired.com — 100% — "3/3" — green blog.example.com — 66% — "2/3" — amber yourbrand.io — 33% — "1/3" — red random.org — 0% — "0/3" — muted Right column (~45% width): "Content Attributes" Header: "Content Attributes" in 28px, muted, uppercase, weight 700, letter-spacing 0.15em, marginBottom 36px. 4 attribute bar rows, 24px gap. Each row: flex row with: Label: 26px, weight 700, white, minWidth 200px, text-align right. Bar: 48px height, bg rgba(255,255,255,0.05), radius 24px, flex 1, overflow hidden. Fill div at target percentage, accent color, opacity 0.8. Percentage: 26px, weight 800, accent color, minWidth 80px. Data: "Structure" — 88% — blue "Depth" — 76% — blue "Citations" — 64% — green "Format" — 72% — amber Animation (relative to phase start): Card container: spring delay 5, translateY from 40px, scale from 0.92. "Authoritative Sources" header: spring delay 20. Domain rows: stagger starting at spring delay 40, each row 15 frames apart (40, 55, 70, 85, 100). Each row fades in + translateX from -40px. Bar fill widths interpolate from 0% to target over 30 frames starting 10 frames after the row appears. Green rows (top 2) get a subtle glow pulse starting at frame 130: box-shadow using Math.sin(frame * 0.15) * 0.3 + 0.7 on opacity. "yourbrand.io" row highlight: at frame 200, a red pulsing border (2px solid rgba(239,68,68,0.5)) fades in around the row, plus a small "⚠" icon (24px) fades in to the left of the domain name. "Content Attributes" header: spring delay 210, translateY from 20px. Attribute bars: stagger starting at spring delay 280, each 18 frames apart (280, 298, 316, 334). Each bar label fades in, then bar fills to percentage over 35 frames. On frames 380-430 (aligning with "depth, citations, or format, and adapt"), each attribute label sequentially brightens (opacity pulses from 0.7 to 1.0 and back) in a 12-frame stagger to create a "callout" effect. PHASE 3 — Track Changes Over Time (Sequence duration: 397 + 17 = 414 frames) One full-width card, vertically centered, card style. Inside: Header: "AI Citation Frequency — Last 12 Weeks" in 32px, muted, weight 700, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.08em, marginBottom 48px. Chart: SVG element, width 100%, height 560px, viewBox "0 0 3000 560", preserveAspectRatio none. 5 horizontal grid lines at y = 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% of chart height. Stroke rgba(255,255,255,0.05), strokeWidth 2. Blue solid line (Competitor A): path through points [(0,75%), (15%,68%), (30%,58%), (45%,46%), (60%,34%), (75%,22%), (90%,12%), (100%,6%)]. These percentages are Y positions (0%=top=most cited, 100%=bottom=least cited). Stroke blue, strokeWidth 8, fill none, round caps and joins. Muted dashed line (You): path through points [(0,82%), (15%,80%), (30%,83%), (45%,84%), (60%,82%), (75%,85%), (90%,83%), (100%,84%)]. Stroke muted, strokeWidth 6, fill none, strokeDasharray "24 12". Both lines draw progressively using an interpolated progress value that maps frame range to 0–1, then filtering visible points. X-axis labels below chart: "Wk 1", "Wk 3", "Wk 5", "Wk 7", "Wk 9", "Wk 12" in 28px muted, weight 600, distributed evenly (justify space-between), marginTop 20px. Large stat callout: Positioned above or overlapping the upper-right of the chart. "40–60%" in 96px, weight 900, white, with a blue text-shadow glow. Below it: "of citations change monthly" in 32px, muted, weight 500. Snapshot vs. Scheduled indicator: "Snapshot" indicator: A vertical dashed line (3px wide, red, dashed 12 8) at ~Wk 5 (x = 40% of chart width), with a label "Snapshot" (24px, red, weight 700) at the top, and a small red X circle (40px diameter, red fill, white X stroke) at the intersection with the blue line. "Scheduled" indicator: A green semi-transparent bar spanning the full chart width (height 100%, bg rgba(74,222,128,0.05), border-top and border-bottom 2px solid rgba(74,222,128,0.2)), with a label "Scheduled monitoring ✓" (24px, green, weight 700) at top-right. Annotation badges below the chart: marginTop 52px, flex row, gap 48px. "Competitor A: cited 12×": blue-tinted badge (bg rgba(0,170,255,0.1), border 1.5px rgba(0,170,255,0.3), radius 16px, padding 20px 40px, 30px blue weight 700). Includes a 40px × 6px solid blue rounded swatch. "You: cited 2×": muted badge (bg rgba(156,163,175,0.08), border 1.5px rgba(156,163,175,0.2), same size). Includes a 40px dashed muted line swatch (repeating-linear-gradient pattern). Animation (relative to phase start): Card: spring delay 5, translateY from 50px. Chart header: spring delay 10. Line draw: interpolate frame range [20, 140] to progress [0, 1], extrapolate clamp both sides. Both lines draw simultaneously. "40–60%" stat: spring delay 80, scale from 0.7. Subtitle spring delay 95. Snapshot indicator: spring delay 160, fade in. The vertical red line and X circle appear. At frame 230, snapshot indicator fades OUT (interpolate opacity from 1 to 0 over frames 230-250). Simultaneously, the "Scheduled" green bar fades IN (spring delay 230). This creates the visual contrast between checking once vs. continuous monitoring. Annotation badges: spring delay 260 and 275, translateY from 20px. PHASE 4 — Regional Data / World Map (Sequence duration: 409 + 17 = 426 frames) World map composition filling most of the safe zone. Map: loading assets/other/world.svg via staticFile(). Positioned absolutely at inset 0, width/height 100%, objectFit contain, opacity 0.4, filter invert(1) sepia(1) saturate(2) hue-rotate(180deg). A radial gradient overlay div sits on top: radial-gradient(ellipse at center, rgba(0,170,255,0.06) 0%, transparent 70%). Three MapPin components positioned absolutely on the map: United States: left 22%, top 40%, delay 40 Germany: left 51%, top 30%, delay 65 Japan: left 80%, top 38%, delay 90 Each MapPin has: A pin dot: 48px circle, bg blue, border 5px rgba(0,170,255,0.4), box-shadow 0 0 36px rgba(0,170,255,0.7), with a 4px × 32px blue stem below (opacity 0.6). A card floating above the pin (visible after frame 45): bg navy (#16213E), border 2.5px rgba(0,170,255,0.45), radius 24px, padding 32px 44px, minWidth 480px. Country name: 30px, blue, weight 800, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.08em, marginBottom 18px. 2 skeleton lines (90% and 70% width, 14px height, opacity 0.2 and 0.15). 2 citation pills stacked with 10px gap: green-tinted (bg rgba(74,222,128,0.08), border 1.5px rgba(74,222,128,0.25), radius 10px, padding 10px 20px, 26px green weight 600). US citations: "techcrunch.com", "wired.com" Germany citations: "spiegel.de", "heise.de" Japan citations: "nikkei.com", "asahi.com" Pin animation: spring with delay = pin's delay value. Scale from 0 + translateY from -30px. Card animation: spring with delay = pin's delay + 35. Scale from 0.7 + translateY from 30px. Footer callout at the bottom of the safe zone: "Same query · Different AI citations · Every market" in 44px, blue, weight 700, inside a card (bg rgba(0,170,255,0.08), border 2px rgba(0,170,255,0.3), radius 20px, padding 32px 96px, centered). Spring delay 250, translateY from 30px. Animation (relative to phase start): Map fades in: spring delay 5, scale from 0.9. US pin: spring delay 40. Germany pin: spring delay 65. Japan pin: spring delay 90. Cards appear: 35 frames after their respective pins. Footer: spring delay 250. PHASE 5 — Closing Statement (Sequence duration: 181 + 17 = 198 frames) Minimal, centered typography. No cards, no charts. Centered vertically and horizontally in the safe zone, flex column, alignItems center, justifyContent center, gap 40px. Line 1: "SEO is no longer just about ranking on page one." in 52px, weight 600, muted color at 0.7 opacity. Spring delay 5, translateY from 30px. Divider: horizontal gradient line, linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, #00AAFF, transparent), 3px height, border-radius 2px. Width interpolates from 0 to 600px starting at frame 15 over 20 frames. Line 2: "It's about being the source LLMs trust enough to cite." in 64px, weight 800, with background: linear-gradient(135deg, #FFFFFF 0%, #00AAFF 100%), WebkitBackgroundClip text, WebkitTextFillColor transparent. Spring delay 30, translateY from 30px, scale from 0.92. Use a slightly softer spring (damping 200 is fine, but delay the appearance for gravitas). Subtle glow on line 2 after it settles: textShadow: 0 0 ${40 + Math.sin(frame * 0.1) * 20}px rgba(0,170,255,0.3) — very gentle pulse. CLOSING BLACK (Sequence duration: 20 frames) Fades in from Phase 5 via the standard 17-frame fade transition. TransitionSeries structure: Sequence: Phase 1 (467 frames) Transition: fade, 17 frames Sequence: Phase 2 (497 frames) Transition: fade, 17 frames Sequence: Phase 3 (414 frames) Transition: fade, 17 frames Sequence: Phase 4 (426 frames) Transition: fade, 17 frames Sequence: Phase 5 (198 frames) Transition: fade, 17 frames Sequence: Black (20 frames) Use TransitionSeries from @remotion/transitions with fade() and linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 17 }) for all transitions. Each phase is its own React component. Use useCurrentFrame() and useVideoConfig() inside each. All spring calls use spring({ frame, fps, delay: N, config: { damping: 200 } }). All progressive animations use interpolate() with extrapolateLeft: "clamp" and extrapolateRight: "clamp".

scriptWithTimestamps: 00:05:15:17 - 00:05:18:15 First, compare how the three engines answer the same query.  00:05:18:15 - 00:05:23:14 You might find that Google AI Mode cites your competitor's blog post, Perplexity  00:05:23:19 - 00:05:28:12 pulls from a completely different source, and ChatGPT doesn't mention either of you.  00:05:29:04 - 00:05:33:00 That tells you exactly where your gaps are and where the opportunities lie.  00:05:33:17 - 00:05:36:06 Second, look at the sources.  00:05:36:06 - 00:05:39:15 Which domains keep showing up across all three engines?  00:05:39:16 - 00:05:42:16 Those are the authoritative sources for your topic.  00:05:42:16 - 00:05:45:06 If you're not among them, analyze why.  00:05:45:06 - 00:05:49:05 Figure out what those pages are doing differently, whether it's structure,  00:05:49:05 - 00:05:52:05 depth, citations, or format, and adapt.  00:05:52:12 - 00:05:55:03 Third, track changes over time.  00:05:55:03 - 00:05:57:05 AI answers are volatile.  00:05:57:05 - 00:06:01:09 Research shows that forty to sixty percent of citations change month to month.  00:06:02:00 - 00:06:05:01 If you're only checking once, you're only seeing a snapshot.  00:06:05:09 - 00:06:07:17 Scheduled runs give you the full picture.  00:06:07:17 - 00:06:10:08 And finally, use the regional data.  00:06:10:08 - 00:06:13:16 A query might return completely different AI answers  00:06:13:16 - 00:06:16:16 in the US versus Germany versus Japan.  00:06:17:04 - 00:06:20:09 If you're running international campaigns, this is how you catch  00:06:20:09 - 00:06:23:09 localization issues before they hurt your traffic.  00:06:23:22 - 00:06:26:22 SEO is no longer just about ranking on page one.  00:06:27:06 - 00:06:30:11 It's about being the source that LLMs trust enough to cite.
